en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
The illustrious Mahādeva said:
"Salutations be to Rāma, who is accompanied by his Śakti, and who is as dark and tender as a blue lotus."
To him adorned with a crown, necklaces, and armlets, seated upon a throne, and possessing great splendor. || 1 ||

You are the one, devoid of beginning, middle, and end; you create, preserve, and dissolve the multitude of worlds through your own māyā. Yet you are not tainted by it, for you are blameless and eternally delighted in your own blissful face.

Enveloped by the qualities (guṇas), you perform divine play for the sake of conforming to those devotees who have sought refuge; through various incarnations as gods, humans, and others, you are perceived eternally only by the wise.
Having created the entire world by means of your own portion, you, as the Lord of Serpents, sustain it from below;
above and below, in the forms of the sun, the wind, the moon, medicinal herbs, and the rain-cloud, you dwell in manifold ways throughout the universe.
In this world, you, in the form of fire, incessantly cook all the food of embodied beings;
with the wind as your assistant in the form of a churning stick, you sustain the entire universe by means of this [fire].
O Lord, that splendor of yours which resides in the midst of the moon, the sun, and fire pervades all bodies;
it is from this that the fortitude and the entirety of the mere valor of embodied beings here arise—this is your own essence.
O Lord, though you appear as if distinct to disputants through the divisions of Viriñci, Śiva, and Viṣṇu, or through the distinctions of time, karma, the moon, and the sun,
you are certainly determined here to be the one non-dual Brahman.

Just as You alone are heard of in the Purāṇas and are well-known in the world in the forms of the Fish and others, even so, O Compassionate One, everything exists as a division of You; nothing else appears apart from You.

Whatever has arisen in the infinite creation, whatever will arise, and whatever is currently existing—among the moving and the stationary and all else—that is not seen without you; therefore, you are higher than the highest.
Therefore, all these people do not know the reality of yourself and the Supreme Self due to your illusory power;
however, for those whose minds are purified by the service of your devotees, that one supreme, divine reality shines forth.
Brahmā and the other gods, being preoccupied with external objects, do not know your true nature, which is the reality of the conscious self;
therefore, the wise man, worshipping you with devotion in this very form, attains liberation and becomes free from suffering.
O Lord, having attained my purpose through your name and qualities, I dwell eternally with Bhavānī in Kāśī;
for you who are about to die, I shall impart the mantra of your name, Rāma, for the sake of liberation.
Those who indeed constantly hear, sing, or write this hymn with undivided devotion—may they, having attained all happiness and the supreme state, go to Your abode through Your grace. (13)
Thus ends the Śrīmad-adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, the hymn to Rāma composed by the illustrious Mahādeva.
